summary.text: Alison Waters is the Family First candidate for Gippsland East at the 2026 Victorian state election, as named on both the party's Victorian candidate list and the ABC election guide. Neither Family First nor the ABC had published a biography as at early November 2026.

sources.title: Gippsland East, 2026 Victorian election guide, ABC News
2026 Victorian State Election candidates, Family First Party

summary.text: Amy Espeseth is standing for the Victorian Socialists in Gippsland East at the 2026 Victorian election. Originally from a country area of Wisconsin in the United States, she moved to Australia late in the 1990s and has taught creative writing, literature and publishing at university. In 2009 she received the Victorian Premier's award for an unpublished manuscript, for Sufficient Grace, and the ABC says her latest job was as a Census Engagement Manager with the Australian Bureau of Statistics.

occupation.text: Census Engagement Manager, Australian Bureau of Statistics
occupation.note: The ABC calls this her most recent role; it doesn't say whether she still holds it.

prior_roles.note: The ABC calls this her most recent role but doesn't say whether it is current.

prior_roles.role: University lecturer in creative writing, literature and publishing

priorities.text: My ideas aren't radical. They're rural common sense.
Capping rents and building public housing in the communities where people work
Free public childcare, five days a week
Zero carbon emissions by 2035, with no new fossil fuel projects and support for affected workers
Free, reliable public transport and public ownership of essential services

sources.title: Gippsland East: 2026 Victorian election guide, ABC News
Victorian Premier's Unpublished Manuscript Award, Wikipedia

summary.text: Ash Munro is the Greens candidate for Gippsland East at the 2026 Victorian election. The ABC lists her as a public servant with the Victorian Department of Health who has also been a youth worker and was chair of East Gippsland's Centre of Excellence for Aboriginal Health. On the party's site she says she works, studies and is raising her children in East Gippsland.

occupation.text: Public servant, Victorian Department of Health

prior_roles.organisation: Centre of Excellence for Aboriginal Health East Gippsland

priorities.text: I simply want better for our region
Relief from rising living costs and housing pressure in East Gippsland
Responding to the effects of climate change on the region
Making sure government services reach people living in East Gippsland
Policies built on fairness, community wellbeing and connection to Country

sources.title: Gippsland East: 2026 Victorian election guide, ABC News
Ash Munro, Candidate for Gippsland East, Australian Greens

summary.text: Gemma Rendell is the Nationals candidate for Gippsland East at the 2026 Victorian election, where the party's Tim Bull is retiring. She is a teacher from Bairnsdale, where she and her partner are raising their young daughter, and was born in East Gippsland. Her party page also describes her as a farmer and community volunteer.

priorities.text: I want to deliver a safer, fairer and more affordable regional Victoria.
A fairer share of state government funding for regional areas
Better essential services for people of every age
Extra funding for East Gippsland's roads, hospitals, emergency services and infrastructure
Giving young people in the region the chance to learn skills for life

sources.title: Gippsland East: 2026 Victorian election guide, ABC News
Gemma Rendell, Candidate for Gippsland East, The Nationals Victoria

summary.text: Ricky Muir is the Shooters, Fishers and Farmers candidate for Gippsland East at the 2026 Victorian election. He sat in the Senate for Victoria between 2014 and 2016, having won his seat at the 2013 federal election for the Australian Motoring Enthusiast Party, and was defeated at the 2016 double dissolution. Since joining the Shooters, Fishers and Farmers in 2017 he has run for Morwell in 2018, the Senate in 2019 and Gippsland East in 2022.

previous_candidacies.note: Stood for the Australian Motoring Enthusiast Party.
Stood for the Australian Motoring Enthusiast Party.

legal_and_integrity.text: The Victorian branch of the Australian Motoring Enthusiast Party voted to expel him while it was also voting to disband itself.
legal_and_integrity.outcome: The party's federal body did not recognise the expulsion; he stayed in the Senate until 2016.

sources.title: Gippsland East: 2026 Victorian election guide, ABC News

summary.text: Sonny Stephens is standing for Labor in Gippsland East at the 2026 Victorian election. The ABC describes her as a farmer and agribusiness manager with three years of army service and past work in public health. Apart from her time in the army she has always lived in Gippsland, and in 2025 she stood for Labor in the federal seat of Gippsland.

prior_roles.note: The ABC says she has worked in public health but gives no role or dates, or whether she still does.

summary.text: Steve Goodman is One Nation's candidate for Gippsland East at the 2026 Victorian election. He now lives on his rural property at Tinamba after a working life that, according to the ABC, has taken in forestry, work as a fitter and large earthmoving and construction jobs in Western Australia. He grew up on a dairy farm run by his family in Gippsland.

sources.title: Gippsland East: 2026 Victorian election guide, ABC News
